newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps flat except weaker mogas, naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps flat except weaker mogas, naphtha.

text.p: NWE oil swaps were barely changed on Monday in a particularly slow start to the week, except for $2 losses on gasoline and around $1 on naphtha.
Brent CFDs were flat and typically uneventful for a Monday, although a September 8-12 deal was seen at minus 27 cents.

Gas oil cracks and gas oil and jet differentials were all seen unchanged on lack of interest, as brokers placed 0.2 diesel at $1-$1.75 for September and $2.50-$3 for fourth quarter and EN590 at $5-$5.5 for September and $8.25-$9 for the fourth quarter.
Jet differentials were seen mostly unchanged, although fourth quarter talk was $0.25 lower at $23.75-$24.25, brokers said.
High sulphur fuel oil swaps were marked down by around $0.50 for September and October to $94-$94.50 and $95-$95.50 respectively as a physical barge deal was seen done at $94.50.
But low sulphur values were seen slightly higher at $98-$99 for September and around $100 for October amid September low/high bid talk at $4.
Fourth quarter and beyond, especially for high sulphur, were also seen up amidst extremely thin trading.
Weaker gasoline sentiment saw the September crack talked lower, with offers at $5.05 and bidding rumoured at $4.85, while the fourth quarter was valued at $3.14-$3.45.
Fourth quarter outrights were placed in the $185.50-$187.50 range, with September and October values $2 down on the day at $197.50-$199.50 and around $189 respectively.
Naphtha swaps slipped with lower crude futures by around $1 to $185.50-$186.50 for September and $185-$186 for both October and November.
